nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Fe3O4 and Cu-Fe3O4
nodes.procedure: Fe3O4 and Cu-Fe3O4 catalysts are grown through simple hydrothermal reaction(s) on iron foam (IF) substrate, of which thickness is 2 mm. Cu atoms and oxygen vacancies are introduced into Fe3O4 (Cu-Fe3O4) by the means of a hydrothermal method.
nodes.source_text: In the step, a Cu-Fe3O4 precursor is grown through a simple hydrothermal reaction on an iron foam (IF) substrate... Cu atoms and oxygen vacancies are introduced into Fe3O4 (Cu-Fe3O4) by the means of a hydrothermal method.

nodes.name: Electrochemical activation
nodes.procedure: A subsequent electrochemical activation process (e.g., under -120 mV vs. RHE in 1 M KOH) results in the formation of FeOOH on the surface of the Cu-Fe3O4 precursor, namely the generation of a Cu-FeOOH/Fe3O4 catalyst. This potential-driven electrochemical self-reconstruction follows a dynamic 'dissolution-redeposition' route. In more detail, partial Fe species in the Cu-Fe3O4 precursor leaches at the catalyst-electrolyte interface and subsequently reacts with OH⁻ ions, leading to the electrosynthesis of FeOOH on the surface of the Cu-Fe3O4 precursor.

nodes.source_text: A subsequent electrochemical activation process (e.g., under -120 mV vs. RHE in 1 M KOH) results in the formation of FeOOH on the surface of the Cu-Fe3O4 precursor...

nodes.source_text: A continuous current-time measurement on the Cu-Fe3O4 catalyst... reveals a dramatically increase at −120 mV (vs. RHE), approximately 100% after the application of 50 h activation time... The change of current density is negligible when the activation time is longer than 50 h

nodes.characterization_summary: IF substrate shows continuous 3D porous structure; Fe₃O₄ nanosheets ≈0.5 μm thick; Cu-Fe₃O₄ nanosheets ≈1 μm thick; Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ shows polygon nanoflakes ≈20 nm thick, 3 μm high.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From recorded scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of the as-mentioned catalysts, one can see that the untreated IF substrate owns a continuous 3D porous structure (Figure 1b)... The as-synthesized Fe₃O₄ and Cu-Fe₃O₄ catalysts are ultra-thin and uniform. These nanosheets have an average thickness of ≈0.5 μm (Figure 1c) and 1 μm (Figure 1d), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu-Fe₃O₄ shows lattice fringe spacing of 0.25 nm indexed to (311) plane of Fe₃O₄; Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ shows d-spacings of 0.25 nm (311) and 0.33 nm (310) for Fe₃O₄ and FeOOH with 0.32% lattice mismatch.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The denoted lattice fringe with a spacing of 0.25 nm (Figure 1h) is indexed to the (311) plane of Fe₃O₄. The d spacings of 0.25 and 0.33 nm (Figure 1i) match well with the (311) and (310) lattice planes of Fe₃O₄ and FeOOH, respectively.

properties.description: Total Density of States for Cu-FeOOH/Fe2O3

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe₃O₄, Cu-Fe₃O₄, and Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ show peaks at 30.2°, 35.6°, 62.9° for (220), (311), (440) Fe₃O₄; Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ additionally shows 26.7°, 34.1°, 46.7° for (310), (400), (411) FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks located at 30.2°, 35.6°, and 62.9° (Figure 2a) are indexed to (220), (311), and (440) facets of the standard Fe₃O₄ (PDF#39-1346) in Fe₃O₄, Cu-Fe₃O₄, and Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ catalysts, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: All three catalysts show Fe₃O₄ vibrations at 603 and 657 cm⁻¹; Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ shows additional FeOOH peaks at 240, 302, and 420 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman peaks located at around 603 and 657 cm⁻¹ for three catalysts are in good agreement with the vibrations of Fe₃O₄. The characteristic peaks at 240, 302, and 420 cm⁻¹ in the Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ catalyst can be assigned to the reported typical vibrations of FeOOH.

properties.description: Synthesis method involving Cu and Fe

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu-Fe₃O₄ and Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ show signal at g=2.003 confirming oxygen vacancies; Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ shows amplified and broadened signal indicating increased oxygen vacancy concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra of both Cu-Fe₃O₄ and Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ catalysts exhibit a typical signal at g = 2.003, confirming the existence of oxygen vacancies (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s shows peaks at 529.7 eV (Cu/Fe-O), 530.9 eV (oxygen vacancies), 532.8 eV (surface oxygen); Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ at 710.0, 711.6, 721.8, 724.2 eV; Cu 2p₃/₂ shows Cu⁰/Cu⁺ at 933.1 eV, Cu²⁺ at 934.9 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the O 1s XPS spectra of these catalysts, three peaks can be identified (Figure 2d). The peak at about 529.7 eV is attributed to the Cu/Fe-O bond, while the peak at about 530.9 eV corresponds to the oxygen vacancies...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 7.3 mF cm⁻² for Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄, 2.4 mF cm⁻² for Cu-Fe₃O₄, 2.3 mF cm⁻² for Fe₃O₄, 4.8 mF cm⁻² for Pt/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The estimated Cdl of a Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ catalyst is 7.3 mF cm⁻² (Figure 4d), larger than that of Pt/C (4.8 mF cm⁻²), Cu-Fe₃O₄ (2.4 mF cm⁻²) and Fe₃O₄ (2.3 mF cm⁻²) catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ shows smallest charge transfer resistance among Fe₃O₄, Cu-Fe₃O₄, and Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The recorded Nyquist plot of the Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ catalyst exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance within these three catalysts, demonstrating its outstanding charge transfer during the HER process.

nodes.characterization_summary: IF substrate Fe = 99.432 wt%, Ni = 0.401 wt%; separated IF from Cu-Fe₃O₄ has Ni = 0.436 wt%; separated IF from Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ has Ni = 0.437 wt%; separated catalyst powders show minimal Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contents of Fe and other impurities in IF were determined by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). The obtained mass fraction of Fe is 99.432 wt.% (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES shows lower white line intensity and negative absorption edge shift in Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ vs Cu-Fe₃O₄ indicating decreased Fe valence; FT-EXAFS shows Fe-O at 1.51 Å, Fe-Fe/Cu at 2.61 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra of Fe₃O₄, Cu-Fe₃O₄ and Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ catalysts (Figure 3a) were studied... The white line intensities of both Cu-FeOOH/Fe₃O₄ and Cu-Fe₃O₄ catalysts are lower than that of a Fe₃O₄ catalyst.
